Case study (descriptive): Google, CSA, GovTech and IMDA ran a sandbox testing computer-use agents for three potential public-sector uses (automated QA of government digital services, automated AI safety testing of third-party chatbots, social assistance applications). Lessons: use realistic test data and environments; log and evaluate the agent's reasoning at each step; identify use-case-specific attack vectors such as indirect prompt injection; keep humans in the loop during testing. Findings: the agent included extraneous personal details in a significant number of cases and in some instances navigated to arbitrary URLs when instructed by injected content.
